pr_title: Fix `Path` and `Exception` content in the Problem Details Json
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/43816

## Description

`Developer Exception Middleware` generates a Problem Details with `Request Path` as `object`. This change update it to a `string`.

## Customer Impact

In Preview 7, the `Developer Exception Middleware` was updated to generate a Problem Details, all exception information including the `Request Path`.

``` json
"path": {
    "value": "/throw",
    "hasValue": true
}
```

With this change the `Problem Details` json payload will contains `Path` as `string` instead of `object`.

``` json
"path":  "/throw"
```

## Regression?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

It is actually a bug fix.

## Risk

- [ ] High
- [ ] Medium
- [x] Low

Very low risk, we're just fixing the generated Problem Details content introduced in .NET 7 Preview 7.

## Verification

- [X] Manual (required)
- [ ] Automated

## Packaging changes reviewed?

- [ ] Yes
- [ ] No
- [x] N/A

@brunolins16 if the header values are serialized as arrays (to support distinct multi-values) shouldn't the values there that have comma-separation appear as separate entries in the arrays? Perhaps it's better to just serialize the header values as strings.

> @brunolins16 if the header values are serialized as arrays (to support distinct multi-values) shouldn't the values there that have comma-separation appear as separate entries in the arrays? Perhaps it's better to just serialize the header values as strings.

@DamianEdwards it looks like the headers are being serialized the same way they were received from the client. I don't recommend trying to parse them into separate values if the client didn't send them that way. `User-Agent` shows why that would be non-trivial.

> @brunolins16 if the header values are serialized as arrays (to support distinct multi-values) shouldn't the values there that have comma-separation appear as separate entries in the arrays? Perhaps it's better to just serialize the header values as strings.

Not sure, because If i have multiple times the same header and it serializes correctly, eg.:

``` json
"Accept-Encoding": [
    "gzip, deflate, br",
    "custom"
]
```

So the array is there to support when headers are defined more than once? Seems like the wrong optimization given how uncommon that is. Could we make it only serialize as array if there are actually multiple headers via a simple projection?
It's not even a deliberate choice at the moment, that's just how we represent headers on the server. If we want to consolidate to a single string for this debug output that's fine.
